key_insight: Fault-tolerant bosonic sensing preserves Heisenberg-limited time scaling for displacement estimation under dephasing, extending the useful interrogation window beyond the unprotected limit.
engineering_relevance: The protocol offers a route to noise-resilient bosonic quantum sensors by coupling probes to error-corrected qubit registers.
method: Construct an optimal error-correcting code under a mean photon-number constraint.
Use controlled displacements to couple the bosonic probe to a repetition-encoded qubit register.
Repeat boson-parity measurements and resets to remove probe noise while preserving the stored logical phase.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical scaling: distance-d encoding suppresses logical failures to order p^((d+1)/2), enabling Fisher information proportional to NT² over times of order γ_A^(-(d+1)/2), versus order γ_A^(-1) without fault tolerance.
watch_item: The scaling requires sufficiently small residual signals and is analyzed under circuit-level bit-flip noise; broader hardware-error robustness remains an implementation concern.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Metrology with Bosonic Probes
